# dsh-context-annotations
**English** · 中文

A DSH (DeepSeek Harness) Web GUI plugin: select any text in the conversation,
write a note about it,

and let the whole batch ride along with your next message
— for that one round only.
This repository carries the `dsh-plugin` topic, which the DeepSeek Harness documentation requires of
plugin repositories so they can be discovered; the link above is the inline, clickable form of that
itories so they can be discovered; the link above is the inline, clickable form of that requirement.
## What it does

1. **Select → annotate.** Select text anywhere in the conversation (a reply, a
tool card, your own m

essage), and a floating **注释** button appears beside the
selection. Click it, type the note, press *

*Enter**. Shift+Enter breaks the
line, Escape cancels.
2. **Collect several.** Every saved note beco

mes a numbered marker at the left
edge of the passage it is about — **hovering a marker shows that n

ote** — and a
**N 条注释** strip appears above the composer. Click the strip to open the
pending batch,

where each annotation shows its quoted passage and note with
edit and delete actions. Clicking a ma

rker opens that note's editor, with a
delete button.
3. **Send together.** Your message gains one sh

ort **“💬 N 条注释”** bubble; the
annotation text never appears in the conversation. **Hover that bubble

** to see
exactly which passages the batch quoted and what each note says. The list
reaches the mode

l as a system-prompt section, so the request still carries
every quoted passage and note. The batch

is consumed once and its markers stay
in the transcript, dimmed.
4. **Send alone.** With an empty co

mposer, the strip's send button starts a round
from the annotations alone — no typed text required.

That round carries the
same `💬 N 条注释` pill as its own message, so the transcript looks no
different
from a batch that rode a typed message.
## How it works
The browser half owns the editing UI; the Host half owns delivery.

- The browser posts the complete batch to `/api/dsh-context-annotations`
(a route registered through

`ctx.connection.fetch`, behind the carrier's trust
fence). It never writes into the draft.
- The Ho

st keeps that batch per Session and listens on the `agent/pre-step`
waterfall. `pre-step` hands over

exactly the messages the step claimed — never
replayed history — so a batch can only ride one round

. When the step carries a
`source.kind === "user"` message, the Host appends one extra message that

holds
only the marker (`💬 N 条注释`) and leaves the human message byte-for-byte
unchanged.
- The annota

tion text does not travel in a message: `ctx.systemPrompt.section()`
contributes it to the prompt, a

nd the rendered prompt is logged as a hidden
`system/message` node. The conversation therefore shows

one short bubble while
the request carries the full list; both are reconstructable from the log, an

d
no plugin event type is invented.
- The marker message is written before the step records its mess

ages, so it is
part of an ordinary `user/message` record, and the prompt is likewise
reconstructable

from the log. By design, fork, resume and replay should
reproduce the conversation the model saw; n

o plugin event type is invented.
- A round needs a message body, and the shipped submit path ignores

an empty
draft. With nothing typed (and no attachment), the strip therefore writes the
batch pill i

nto the composer and submits once that write is visible — the same
path a typed message takes. The H

ost recognises the pill-shaped body as “this
round *is* the batch”, consumes it and appends no secon

d pill. A pill the round
did not take (a refused submit, or a write that only reached the composer a

fter
the strip stopped waiting) is cleared again after a short grace period, so the
plugin does not

leave text behind that the user never typed. The strip stays
armed until the batch's consumption is

observed, so a second click in that
window cannot start a duplicate round.

## Configuration

The bundle currently reads no configuration. The folded list carries no marker
line, so it reads as
the user's own numbered notes rather than a plugin block.

## Limits

- Markers key on character offsets into the flattened conversation text and are
validated against th

e recorded passage; when that offset no longer matches (the
content above the passage changed), a wh

itespace-insensitive passage search
takes over, disambiguated by the passage's occurrence ordinal. T

the note itself stays in the strip and is still sent. Markers that
would land on the same box are n

udged upwards so they do not stack.
- Annotations live in Host memory per Session. A Host restart dr

ops a pending
batch (the browser adopts only what the Host still holds).
